questions.stem: A FortiGate neighbor stays Active and debug reports 107. Which protocol exchange has not completed?
choices: The TCP three-way handshake to peer port 179
The BGP OPEN capability negotiation between peers
The first UPDATE carrying accepted prefixes
The route-map evaluation for received networks
feedback: Correct: Active plus error 107 marks an incomplete TCP handshake before BGP OPEN can begin.
OPEN follows TCP establishment; an OPEN failure occurs after the transport socket exists.
UPDATE exchange is later; prefixes cannot be exchanged before the session is Established.
Route maps govern route policy after BGP messages arrive; they do not complete TCP transport.

questions.stem: The route to a BGP peer exists, but capture shows repeated SYN packets without SYN-ACK. What should be checked next?
choices: The inbound prefix-list permit sequence
The return route and any filter for TCP/179
The maximum-prefix threshold on received routes
The route-map set-local-preference action
feedback: A prefix list is evaluated for route updates, not for the missing TCP response.
Correct: the missing SYN-ACK points to the remote return path, an ACL, or a listener/filter problem.
Maximum-prefix is enforced after routes are exchanged and cannot explain an incomplete handshake.
Local preference is assigned to received routes after BGP reaches the update stage.

questions.stem: A multihop eBGP peer is reachable through a routed core. Which neighbor settings address the local source and hop behavior?
choices: Set passive and change the router ID
Set route-map-in and soft-reconfiguration
Set update-source and enable eBGP multihop with a suitable TTL
Set next-hop-self and remove the remote AS
feedback: Passive changes who initiates a session; it does not select the intended local source or permit multihop.
Route-map and soft-reconfiguration affect route processing, not TCP source identity or TTL.
Correct: update-source selects the local source; multihop and TTL allow the routed peer distance.
Next-hop-self changes advertised next-hop attributes; the remote AS is required for eBGP identity.

questions.stem: The debug shows 104, Connection reset by peer, rather than 107. What does that change in the diagnosis?
choices: It proves the local route table is empty
It proves a route-map rejected every prefix
It proves BGP reached Established and lost keepalives
It indicates the remote side reset the TCP attempt
feedback: A reset does not establish that the local route table is empty; inspect the packet path.
Route-map rejection cannot be inferred from a transport reset before route exchange.
Established-state keepalive loss is a later failure and would show a different state history.
Correct: 104 indicates the peer or an intermediary reset the connection during the attempt.

questions.stem: FortiManager installs a profile to a 2 GB FortiGate and the preview includes udp-not-quic. What is the most useful first comparison?
choices: Compare generated CLI with that model's FortiOS parser support
Compare the destination address object with the firewall policy
Compare the device HA priority with the ADOM revision
Compare the administrator GUI theme with the install owner
feedback: Correct: the defect is a manager-generated attribute unsupported by the target model/build.
Address matching is unrelated to whether the target recognizes a CLI node in an SSL profile.
HA priority and ADOM revision do not determine parser capability for this command.
GUI appearance and task ownership have no bearing on target-side command support.

questions.stem: Why can an SSL/SSH profile save successfully in FortiManager but fail on one FortiGate during install?
choices: The manager skipped the device route lookup
The target parser or platform does not implement the emitted option
The firewall policy has no matching destination service
The device DNS cache has not refreshed QUIC records
feedback: Route lookup is not the relevant validation boundary for a syntax rejection.
Correct: manager-side schema validity does not guarantee target model/build support for every CLI option.
Policy service matching does not explain a parser rejection in the SSL/SSH profile subtree.
DNS cache state does not affect whether the FortiGate accepts a configuration command.

questions.stem: Which distinction matters when reviewing the FortiOS SSL/SSH profile fields?
choices: quic and udp-not-quic are interchangeable block controls
https and dot share one global action with no separate context
quic handles QUIC; udp-not-quic handles matched UDP that is not QUIC
udp-not-quic controls TCP fallback after a QUIC handshake
feedback: The fields have different protocol meanings; treating them as aliases can change inspection behavior.
FortiOS exposes separate https and dot subtrees, so the actions are not one global value.
Correct: udp-not-quic is the action for matched UDP traffic that is not QUIC.
TCP fallback behavior is not what the udp-not-quic field defines.

questions.stem: A workaround works on one target but makes capable models lose intended inspection behavior. What does this suggest?
choices: The entire ADOM must be downgraded immediately
The manager should stop validating every install
The FortiGate routing process is rewriting the profile
The workaround was applied too broadly instead of being model-scoped
feedback: Downgrading the ADOM may create wider compatibility issues and is not the first response.
Validation is needed to expose target differences; disabling it hides evidence.
Routing does not rewrite SSL/SSH profile attributes during installation.
Correct: use a device/model-scoped override and verify affected and unaffected targets.

questions.stem: FortiAnalyzer's Azure output profile validates, but no rows appear in Log Analytics. Which object is still required to activate forwarding?
choices: A Log Forwarding Remote Server setting that references the output profile
A second FortiAnalyzer ADOM revision for the custom table
A FortiGate central SNAT map for the DCE address
A FortiSwitch VLAN mapping for the Azure workspace
feedback: Correct: the profile must be selected by a Remote Server forwarding setting using the output plugin.
An ADOM revision does not activate log forwarding or reference the output profile.
SNAT may be part of network reachability, but it does not attach the forwarding profile.
Switch VLAN mapping has no role in the FortiAnalyzer-to-Azure plugin configuration.

questions.stem: Why does the Azure custom-table transform create TimeGenerated from logtime?
choices: Azure requires the source field to be named logtime
FortiAnalyzer only sends timestamps in local time
The Logs Ingestion API requires a TimeGenerated column in the target schema
The DCE uses TimeGenerated as its client secret
feedback: logtime is only the sample source field; the destination requirement is a separate column.
Time conversion is performed by the DCR transform; the requirement is not simply local time.
Correct: the DCR transform creates the mandatory TimeGenerated field from the source timestamp.
The DCE URL and application secret are separate settings; TimeGenerated is a schema field.

questions.stem: Which six values does the FortiAnalyzer Fluentd Azure profile require?
choices: Workspace name, firewall serial, ADOM name, source port, log type, and username
Tenant ID, client ID, client secret, DCE URL, DCR ID, and table name
DCR name, device ID, interface name, time zone, proxy port, and token cache
Tenant name, DCE secret, log filter, CA certificate, UDP port, and group ID
feedback: These are not the documented Azure Logs Ingestion parameters for the Fluentd profile.
Correct: those are the six required parameters listed in FortiAnalyzer's example.
Device and interface inventory values are not the six plugin credentials and endpoint fields.
The DCE URL is not a DCE secret; the listed values do not match the documented profile.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of variable references such as ${CLIENT_SECRET} in the output profile?
choices: They replace the DCR transformation at ingestion time
They make the App Registration anonymous
They select which FortiGate logs are collected
They avoid placing the literal secret directly in the profile text
feedback: The DCR transform still defines the target schema and TimeGenerated mapping.
Azure still authenticates the application; variable indirection does not remove identity.
Log selection is controlled by forwarding settings and filters, not secret variables.
Correct: the Community tip uses variables to mask values such as the client secret.

questions.stem: Azure returns an ingestion schema error after the token succeeds. Which area deserves attention first?
choices: DCR stream, custom table schema, and TimeGenerated transformation
FortiAnalyzer administrator password expiration
FortiGate BGP neighbor update-source configuration
FortiSwitch VRRP preemption timer
feedback: Correct: successful token acquisition moves the fault boundary toward DCR/table schema and transform.
An admin password does not explain an authenticated ingestion request rejected for schema.
BGP update-source is unrelated to Azure log schema validation.
VRRP preemption does not affect the table schema accepted by Azure.

questions.stem: A FortiSwitch VRRP Master is still sending advertisements, but the upstream route is gone. Which feature addresses this?
choices: Lowering the advertisement interval only
Changing the virtual router ID on the backup
Configuring vrdst to track a critical destination
Disabling the virtual MAC on the primary
feedback: Faster advertisements detect peer failure, not a live Master that has lost upstream reachability.
Changing the VRID breaks group identity rather than monitoring the route.
Correct: vrdst monitors destination reachability and can reduce the Master's priority to zero.
Disabling VMAC can disrupt the shared gateway identity and does not provide route tracking.

questions.stem: What does priority zero in get router info vrrp indicate in the documented route-monitor scenario?
choices: The VRRP group has been deleted
The tracked destination is unreachable and the Master has yielded priority
The backup has a higher interface speed
The virtual IP address has changed to the physical address
feedback: The group remains configured; priority zero is the route-tracking response.
Correct: loss of the monitored destination drives the Master priority to zero.
Interface speed is not the condition shown by the vrdst example.
The virtual IP remains the shared gateway; it does not become the physical address.

questions.stem: Which design choice makes a vrdst monitor useful rather than noisy?
choices: Choose a critical destination reachable through the intended upstream path
Choose a public host that both switches may be unable to ping
Choose the switch's own management address on the same VLAN
Choose a host whose ICMP policy changes frequently
feedback: Correct: the target should represent the path whose loss should trigger gateway failover.
A target unreachable from both peers can make both priorities fall and defeat the design.
The local management address does not test the upstream route being protected.
An unstable ICMP policy can cause false failovers unrelated to actual routing.

questions.stem: Which prerequisite is called out for FortiSwitch VRRP virtual MAC operation?
choices: Enable allow-mac-move on every FS-6xxF first
Use a unique virtual IP on every member
Disable the advanced-features license
Enable vrrp-virtual-mac on all members and check model conflicts
feedback: On some models allow-mac-move conflicts with VMAC; it is not a universal prerequisite.
Members of the same VRRP group share the virtual IP rather than each using a different one.
VRRP requires the advanced-features license; disabling it removes the entitlement.
Correct: VMAC is disabled by default and must be enabled across the group, subject to model limits.

questions.stem: FortiGate manages a FortiAP over IPv6. Which interface permission is required for the wireless fabric management path?
choices: ip6-allowaccess ping only
ip6-allowaccess fabric
allowaccess radius-acct on IPv4
set vrrp-virtual-mac enable
feedback: Ping allows ICMP testing but does not enable the wireless fabric management service.
Correct: Fortinet's IPv6 management example includes fabric in ip6-allowaccess.
RADIUS accounting access is unrelated to AP controller discovery over IPv6.
VRRP VMAC is a gateway feature, not a FortiAP management permission.

questions.stem: Which two methods are documented for FortiAP IPv6 controller discovery?
choices: DNS SRV and static ARP
BGP route reflection and LLDP
IPv6 multicast discovery and DHCPv6 Option 52
SAML redirect and RADIUS CoA
feedback: Those are not the two discovery methods documented for IPv6 AP controller discovery.
Routing and LLDP may support connectivity but are not the discovery mechanisms listed.
Correct: the AP can discover through controller multicast or DHCPv6 Option 52.
SAML and CoA belong to identity workflows, not CAPWAP controller discovery.

questions.stem: What does NP7/NP7lite support that NP6/NP6lite does not in this feature?
choices: CAPWAP data traffic offload for IPv4 and IPv6
DHCPv6 Option 52 address assignment
IPv6 client SLAAC on the wireless SSID
The FortiAP authorization database
feedback: Correct: Fortinet documents CAPWAP data offload on NP7/NP7lite, not NP6/NP6lite.
DHCPv6 Option 52 is a discovery method, not an NPU offload capability.
Client SLAAC is an IPv6 client service and not the documented hardware boundary.
AP authorization is controller logic, not the NPU offload feature.

questions.stem: The AP console shows cwWtpd restarting repeatedly. What is the strongest next step?
choices: RMA the AP because the process name proves hardware failure
Change every SSID to bridge mode
Disable CAPWAP encryption without checking compatibility
Correlate AP firmware, FSM/crash/certificate/power evidence with an on-network CAPWAP capture
feedback: A process restart is a symptom and does not establish a hardware defect.
SSID forwarding mode does not explain a controller process restarting before stable CAPWAP.
Disabling security without evidence is unsafe and may not address the cause.
Correct: collect firmware, FSM, crash, power and certificate evidence plus real network testing.

questions.stem: FortiNAC reports “No EAP session matching state.” What does the message most directly indicate?
choices: The user's password has definitely expired
An EAP packet arrived without a matching active server-side exchange context
The switch VLAN tag is malformed
The endpoint has no IPv6 default route
feedback: Credential failure is possible later, but the message describes missing EAP session context.
Correct: the server received EAP traffic but could not associate it with a live EAP state.
A VLAN error may affect access after authentication but does not explain this EAP state message.
IPv6 routing is unrelated to the RADIUS/EAP session correlation symptom.

questions.stem: In FortiNAC proxy RADIUS mode, what happens to 802.1X EAP authentication?
choices: FortiNAC processes only accounting and drops EAP
FortiNAC converts EAP into SNMP polling
FortiNAC proxies EAP authentication to an external RADIUS server
FortiNAC assigns a VLAN without consulting an authentication service
feedback: Proxy mode is an authentication path, not a policy to drop EAP.
SNMP polling is a separate network-device management mechanism.
Correct: proxy mode handles MAC auth locally and proxies 802.1X EAP to external RADIUS.
VLAN assignment can follow authorization, but it does not replace EAP authentication.

questions.stem: Which prerequisite applies to FortiNAC Local RADIUS EAP authentication?
choices: A server certificate must be installed for EAP
The switch must use BGP multihop
The FortiNAC Manager must share a VRID with the NAS
The DCR table must end in _CL
feedback: Correct: the Local RADIUS guide requires a server certificate for EAP authentication.
BGP multihop is unrelated to the RADIUS EAP service.
VRID is a VRRP identifier, not a RADIUS requirement.
_CL is an Azure table naming convention, not an EAP prerequisite.

questions.stem: The same endpoint succeeds off-peak but intermittently loses EAP state during busy periods. Which hypothesis best matches the forum discussion?
choices: A permanent VLAN mismatch on every port
An invalid AP certificate in all cases
A missing BGP route to the RADIUS server
Delay, load distribution, NAS/supplicant restart, or service load affecting state continuity
feedback: A fixed VLAN error would not normally explain intermittent EAP state correlation.
An AP certificate issue is not established by the EAP session message and affects more than one path.
BGP reachability may affect RADIUS transport, but the stated symptom is a missing active EAP context.
Correct: these are the specific classes of causes raised by Fortinet staff in the recent discussion.

questions.stem: What does FortiNAC Local RADIUS not provide by itself?
choices: EAP authentication for supported methods
RADIUS accounting; accounting can be proxied externally
MAC authentication processing
RADIUS Access-Accept attributes
feedback: Local RADIUS supports documented EAP methods when prerequisites are met.
Correct: Local RADIUS does not provide accounting; it can be proxied externally.
Local RADIUS processes MAC authentication as well as EAP authentication.
FortiNAC can return configured RADIUS attributes in an Access-Accept.
